* Bolt TZ Office no mention in contract. *Correct- the Platform is owned and operated by Bolt Ops OU and as such the offers come from Bolt Ops OU.*

* 2.6 no time frame mentioned for notification. *Yes this is deliberate to give both of us flexibility as Bolt is not paying any money to Nas. We will act reasonably.*
* indemnity clause, need of that? *No. no cash is exchanging hands between us so this is not necessary.* 
* 10 Taxes are to be paid by both parties, in this case, the Bolt Drivers as and when they make a purchase, there is a 18% VAT across Tanzania, which is included in the Invoices (unless they are VAT EXEMPTED, for which we shall need a TRA Stamped VAT Exemption Certificate) [~accountid:5d1b218591943f0d2ac52db0] *Discuss this with him. There are no taxes to be paid by Bolt. No money is being paid by Bolt and therefore no taxes borne by Bolt. Nas is billing the drivers directly as it would any other walk in client for his business so he should provide them with whichever invoices are legally required.*

Dear *Vicki*,

Thank you for your further request which was received by us on *17/6/2024.* Please find the responses below:



* CCTV

Your request for a copy of any CCTV footage in use by our drivers is important to us, and we're here to provide clarification.

*Drivers* are not Bolt’s employees and are designated as independent data controllers under the respective privacy regulations. 

It's important to note that Bolt does not install cameras in vehicles nor require *drivers to have cameras in vehicles.* This signifies that all camera usage by *drivers* is independent of Bolt's knowledge and instruction. Bolt therefore does not process or store any CCTV footage. 



* Communication with the driver

Instant messages between Passengers and Drivers are kept in the Bolt App only until the order is completed and for 3 months after in our systems. Any calls between Passengers and Drivers are not recorded, and therefore no such data is stored or processed by Bolt. 



* Driver’s communication with Bolt

We have to point our that we are not entitled to share any specific measures taken as this information relates to the personal data of another party.



* *Communication between driver, the company, the passenger ?*



Sincerely, 

Customer Support Team

Hey [~accountid:6114faeeae72b2006fd27ba3] , the payment is allocated to the courier’s debt balance, but it is their earning balance that was negative - Now, if they return the bag and we return their 30€ deposit for it, the payment will go to their earnings balance, with the earning balance ending up at 13.55€, which they will receive in their payout and a -16.45€ debt balance, that will stay on their account. This means that Bolt didn’t receive the courier’s payment as it’s sitting on their account as an overpayment, but the courier will also not receive the entire amount of the deposit as they should.

The question is, what is the correct process, should we simply add a manual adjustment of 16.45€ on top of the deposit (so in total 46.45€), as the courier paid the debt, we just allocated it to a different balance and at one point there will be a fix for this issue, or would the correct process be to consider this amount paid, only pay the deposit amount, but then the courier only receives 13.55€ to their bank account and the 16.45€ sits on their courier account as overpayment?

As I can see there is no any Base fee calculator for these cities above, I believe you would like to create them to these cities or what? 

IF yes: 
In order to create base fee calculators, we would need the following information:

* *Commission rate*: Commission percentage that will apply per ride to the driver/fleet.
* *Currency*: Usually country default if not stated otherwise
* *Invoicing strategy*: Driver or Company. This will define to whom payouts will go, and invoices will be issued.
* *Booking fee:* Is there an active booking fee in the city? If so, do you want it to be deducted from the driver (and reflected on the commission invoice), or be a 100% driver income?
* *Cash-blocking thresholds*: Defines the cash ride limits for blocking/unblocking cash rides for a driver. This can be copied from other cities, but please discuss with [{color:#b3f5ff}Billing Analytics{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/1240/create/806] if your market is cash-heavy.
** Max negative balance before messaging: The threshold where we will notify the driver that they are getting closer to being cash-blocked
** Max negative balance before removing cash payments: The debt threshold we allow cash rides up to. After the driver exceeds this threshold, cash orders will be disabled.
** Minimal balance to unblock cash rides: The balance threshold where we will once again unblock the driver’s cash rides.
* *List of company_ids you want this fee calculator to be attached to*.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*What is a Base Fee Calculator*

It is a default fee calculator template created by Billing team in order for local operations teams to easily attach the relevant fee calculator to new companies. [Please read this guide to see how|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/1603928517/Base+fee+calculators].
{panel}

* ir35 - couldn’t/shouldn’t we state that we _don’t provide people resource to deliver easyJet's requirement_?
* The privacy bits both in the questionnaire and in the agreement to be confirmed with Privacy as needed. Same with IT Security. But I also noticed a comment from easyJet in their draft that these bits are not yet final.

Hello!

As [~accountid:5bb1cc64c9dad04734ea835a] mentioned there needs to be a local assessment of this based on the central guidance provided. But to be helpful there are two key things that come to mind on this - particularly if there is any intention of using any _‘ride booker’_-like tool in the UK as we’ve previously been involved in criminal investigations on this.

----

{color:#4c9aff}+*UK Regs:*+{color}

[~accountid:712020:7da8a66c-8a7e-4912-b329-35d94607bdc3] re: regulatory / public policy concerns - are we sure on this? Ultimately, it depends on how the proposal is intended to work - I may have wildly misunderstood but these comments in the ticket makes me raise this:

{quote}*_The client charges the end user (guest) as part of their bill_*

*_To clarify the guest would be paying the hotel as part of there bill for the cost of the ride._*{quote}

I will defer to your team’s understanding of the transport regulatory rules that apply in this market, but my understanding is that _only_ a licensed operator can charge any person for private hire services in England and Wales. If the intention is for a +_hotel_+ to charge guests for transportation services then the hotel ought to have an operator’s licence. This is the reason why the ride booker feature has been historically disabled for business customers in the UK.

However, a hotel could charge a guest a concierge fee for *_arranging_* these services - as for shoe shining services and anything else.

If the current proposal is for the hotel to charge for the transportation services, this needs considering. Bolt could take contractual steps to ensure that these hotels have ‘all relevant consents, licences and permissions' etc., or Bolt could take a view on the basis that this is principally a problem for the hotel… but perhaps our involvement in enabling issues to arise may not be viewed favourably.

_Fun (?) fact: in my first week at Bolt I had a meeting with the TFL police regarding the unlawful use of the ‘ride booker’ tool in the UK - a business ('Purple Express') had booked a ride on behalf of someone else using Bolt business, which was rightly being investigated as a criminal offence as they were charging a passenger a ridiculously high fee directly for a private hire journey - the passenger complained to TfL - and the Bolt Business user didn’t have an operator's licence)._ 

{color:#4c9aff}+*UK Operating Models:*+{color}

As mentioned by [~accountid:5fc110f647ac91006fc4977a] the UK (currently…) operates +_private hire_+ rides on the basic of a ‘*principal model*’ where Bolt charges passengers for transportation services. This set up means that the usual financial regulatory sensitivities that come from Bolt charging customers directly will not apply. This is what has enabled Bolt to launch the passenger service fee in the UK. For more details on this, see note circulated by [~accountid:5bb1cc64c9dad04734ea835a] and the financial regulatory note referred to within 👌. 

_^This must always be assessed on a per market basis but in summary, whenever Bolt operates on its standard ‘_*_agency model_*_’ (i.e. Bolt charges commission) and relies on a ‘commercial agent’-type exemption to avoid needing a financial regulatory licence, charging additional fees directly is going to create some level financial regulatory risk unless Bolt holds a financial regulatory licence in that market. Bolt does not currently hold licences to that effect._

Be mindful that London Black Cabs (and any other ‘true taxi’ services in the UK - where Bolt charges commission) +*do not*+ operate on the ‘principal model’. 

In respect of Bolt Business portal fees, which are obviously a little different, there is a section on this in the fin. reg. note [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cT0_tjXE4e4dniJGBU_T6-A2KHLkasM_0IBdl0EQszg/edit#heading=h.6mc62g6fwlor]. 

----

Thanks all 🙏

Regarding the statute of limitations - perhaps the law is interpreted differently in PT, however, in Estonia, the deadline to start counting the statute of limitation would be the date where insurer rejected the injured party’s claim because that’s when the injured party learned that he has to file a claim to Bolt/Allianz if he wishes compensation. I didn’t notice any mention of what was the date when the claimant received the negative decision from Allianz, however, that was probably a few months after the accident. 

Regarding what can Allianz do for us - the Personal Accident Insurance is a policy that Bolt buys on behalf of its riders, i.e. the insured party is the rider and not Bolt. So the insurance policy has no legal or liability protection for Bolt. For Bolt to receive any legal or liability protection, Bolt would need to buy a corporate general liability policy for the PT entity. These types of policies have been bought “on a need” basis so far (i.e. if needed for licensing/regulatory reasons), as far as I know, there’s no corporate general liability policy in PT. Can you confirm, please, [~accountid:638713ee77acd224b3411ff9] that you have not bought this policy on your own? 🙏

Potentially useful Query for Rolling means:

*Rolling means*

{noformat}WITH base_data AS (
    SELECT 
        date_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN country = 'Portugal' THEN 'Portugal' 
            ELSE city 
        END AS city,
        os AS platform,
        metric_name,
        metric_value
    FROM mart_models.mart_rider_ads_metrics
    WHERE metric_name IN ('1Y GMV Eur', 'First time rides')
    AND os IN ('android', 'ios')
    AND (city IN (SELECT city FROM ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing.rider_rebudgeting_cities) OR country = 'Portugal')
),
aggregated_data AS (
    SELECT date_date, city, platform,
        SUM(CASE WHEN metric_name = '1Y GMV Eur' THEN metric_value ELSE 0 END) AS sum_gmv,
        SUM(CASE WHEN metric_name = 'First time rides' THEN metric_value ELSE 0 END) AS sum_first_time_rides
    FROM base_data
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
),
rolling_avg AS (
    SELECT date_date, city, platform,
        SUM(sum_gmv) OVER (
            PARTITION BY city, platform
            ORDER BY date_date
            ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS rolling_sum_gmv,
        SUM(sum_first_time_rides) OVER (
            PARTITION BY city, platform
            ORDER BY date_date
            ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS rolling_sum_first_time_rides
    FROM aggregated_data
)
SELECT
    date_date, city, platform,
    CASE 
        WHEN rolling_sum_first_time_rides = 0 THEN 0
        ELSE rolling_sum_gmv / rolling_sum_first_time_rides 
    END AS AVG_1Y_GMV
FROM rolling_avg
ORDER BY 1, 2, 3;
{noformat}

# _Are we OK with showing the T&C for Romania after the account is created? The concern might be that we save user account data (email, first name, last name, phone) before the T&C agreement_.

According to the Romanian legislation (GEO 49/2019, art. 25), digital platforms providing ride-hailing services, such as Bolt, must:

* fully and comprehensively inform all users, *upon their registration on the digital platform*, on the terms and conditions of operation of the digital platform, their rights and obligations during and after using the digital platform, as well as regarding the processing of their personal data; the terms and conditions regarding the operation of the digital platform must be easily accessible by users through it, and *the operator must allow to become users of the digital platform* *only those who have expressly agreed to these terms and conditions*;
* process all personal data collected through the digital platform in accordance with the legal provisions in force and to *properly inform, before registration*, all users, through the digital platform, *regarding the collection and processing of their personal data*.

Also, in order to get the licence to operate in Romania, we need to pass and IT audit procedure, which checks if Bolt platforms is fully and comprehensively inform all users, upon their registration on the digital platform, on the terms and conditions of operation of the digital platform, their rights and obligations during and after using the digital platform, as well as regarding the processing of their data personal; and *allows to become users of the digital platform only those who have expressly agreed with these terms and conditions* (Decision 572/2020, art. 6). 

*Thus, we need to show and accept the T&Cs before the account is created*. Fyi - we just had an interview with the IT audit company (one day ago) and it verified that the process is happening according to the above indications.

If any specific questions about the above, please reach out to me. Happy to share the considerations and my findings in more detail. *Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *07.06.2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that the rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;

* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and

*Your rights*

Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

Hey!

I am not 100% sure, but we are using both the speed reporting and GPS data, but I think they are for different purposes. As the IOT device is directly in communication with the vehicle’s onboard computer, this data point is reported and not measured. Essentially - a sensor on the wheel bearing calculates the approximate speed of the vehicle and shouts it to the system (54 km/h). This information is also displayed on the speedometer/HUD and our IOT reports this data back to us (at that time, the speed of the vehicle was 54 km/h). We combine this with location data (at that location the speed limit was 30 km/h) and thus we can determine if the person was speeding.

The distance between the points is determined by the GPS coordinates (the route, the basis for trip calculation).

Yes, the vehicle’s speed sensor usually reports faster speeds, depending on the actual speed, and the size of the rims and tires, this can vary up to 10 km/h. Essentially - the speedometer reads 100 km/h, but if someone were measuring the actual movement speed, it would be somewhere ~93 km/h. The tl;dr is that the operations team is using a speed buffer for speeding fines. If we are saying a person was speeding +40 km/h, it is safe to assume, the speedometer read like +50 km/h.

Anyways - if you have any questions, write me in Slack, and let’s see what can be done 🙂

# Whether we will be collecting any new forms of user (driver/passenger) data relating to Bolt Plus?

Not really, we are offering benefit to users (like in discount campaigns), and only additional data we'd be getting would be related to subscription status e.g. if user is subscribed or not.

# Whether we will be partnering with any new 3rd parties to provide Bolt Plus or any of its benefits?

possibly in the future, but nothing immediate planned at the moment.

# What form the targeted campaigns will take?

Here are the main types of campaigns - 1) temporary price adjustment of subscription (such as cancellation campaigns - if user wants to cancel, give them discount on additional months), 2) temporary time period adjustment of subscription, if user wants to pause campaign for x months, 3) offer additional benefits to user for a limited time. / Potentially in the future we may also drive some conditional campaigns wherein user will be offered some sort of benefit.*On your second query*:

# What vertical/s do these surveys relate to?

mostly rides, but also x-vertical.

# What are the surveys about?

it's to understand primarily the user perception around current subscription benefits and to investigate additional painpoints & benefits they'd like.

look at their data such as rides frequency, etc. in order to group them when looking at survey results. This would allow us to have accurate/objective data behind it instead of bias that could potentially come from depending on answers from participants. For example, if we ask users how frequently they use Bolt in survey, for whatever reason they can answer 'daily' but with data we can see if the user actually only rides X times per month. Objective data would help us analyze findings to see if we can spot any patterns that we can use towards survey result analysis. So that's why I wanted to ideally link them.

Here are the main types of campaigns - 1) temporary price adjustment of subscription (such as cancellation campaigns - if user wants to cancel, give them discount on additional months), 2) temporary time period adjustment of subscription, if user wants to pause campaign for x months, 3) offer additional benefits to user for a limited time. / Potentially in the future we may also drive some conditional campaigns wherein user will be offered some sort of benefit.*On your second query*:

# What vertical/s do these surveys relate to?

mostly rides, but also x-vertical.

# What are the surveys about?

it's to understand primarily the user perception around current subscription benefits and to investigate additional painpoints & benefits they'd like.

# Are these surveys already completed? If so, did we tell Users that results will be anonymous/aggregated by any chance? This is something important we need to look at.

no we'd like to circulate soon in April, you can see the draft under 'Details' section in [this doc|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Omx1PlZRxMbJ_7y7DzJBGmRtq9arUzDGFI0-fBrZ1tM/edit]. I'm reaching out to check with you what we need to communicate to users (also would need to check w legal as well maybe?)

# What do we want to do after connecting the User ID with the Survey result?

look at their data such as rides frequency, etc. in order to group them when looking at survey results. This would allow us to have accurate/objective data behind it instead of bias that could potentially come from depending on answers from participants. For example, if we ask users how frequently they use Bolt in survey, for whatever reason they can answer 'daily' but with data we can see if the user actually only rides X times per month. Objective data would help us analyze findings to see if we can spot any patterns that we can use towards survey result analysis. So that's why I wanted to ideally link them.

Thanks!

First, I would like to explain the process for physical mail handling at the Lisbon Hub:

* Unregistered Mail addressed to _Bolt Support Services PT Unipessoal Lda_ is received by the building’s reception staff (building management’s staff) and then delivered only to the Workplace Experience team.
* Registered Mail addressed to _Bolt Support Services PT Unipessoal Lda_ is only received by a Bolt employee (mostly the Workplace Experience team for general mail and Rentals Ops team for city fines related to Rentals operations in the cities).

Once the Workplace Experience team has (either unregistered or registered) mail in their possession, they will read the content to find out to which team at Bolt that mail concerns and make the relevant forwarding in person to the stakeholder of that team.

For Rides-related mail, the process agreed upon as of June 1 2024 between the Workplace Experience team and the CS-Rides team is:

# The Workplace Experience team receives the physical mail.
# The Workplace Experience team notifies the CS-Rides team via Slack that there’s mail to be collected.
# The CS-Rides team collects and deals with the content according to the internal processes relevant to their line of business.

Hi [~accountid:5eb3683b021ae30ba8320ea6], just to let you know I have researched what to do in the case of unsourced lines in an requisition. 
First thing: open the Buyer’s Hub and then follow the red squares to get to the Requisition Sourcing Console like this, press OK.

!image-20240628-124302.png|width=329,height=372,alt="image-20240628-124302.png"!

Once the report is generated it will show you all of the unsourced REQ and how many lines each one has. You can then click on “Open” to check unsourced lines. 

!image-20240628-124524.png|width=635,height=174,alt="image-20240628-124524.png"!

This will enable you to have full overview of the “opened” requisitions. 

To completely close the requisitions that have unsourced goods lines please run the following task: “*Mass Close Procurement Documents*”. You can find it in Buyer’s Hub or by searching in the search bar.


!image-20240628-124741.png|width=682,height=156,alt="image-20240628-124741.png"!

Once you open the task, populate it like in the screenshot below. 

!image-20240628-124834.png|width=191,height=124,alt="image-20240628-124834.png"!

Once you click on the “requisition”, you will get this pop-up text below where you can filter the results you wish to have. I suggest you use field in the second row: “Requisition”. 

!image-20240628-124918.png|width=567,height=260,alt="image-20240628-124918.png"!

Once task has been completed, the requisition will change the state and you won’t be able to source goods lines anymore.

Hey, [~accountid:712020:f63df97f-cad1-4718-9bb1-80038488d7e2]! Thank you for your patience! Here are my thoughts:

# Currently, CZ, SK, PL and RO are markets where reclassification risk is not yet critical, although not low either. When considering this issue I have had these considerations in mind:
## These markets are fleet markets (most of the couriers belong to fleets) - hence our reclassification risk is lower provided that we communicate our decisions appropriately through fleets. However, we also should not penalise individual couriers and allow fleets to deal with their couriers as they see fit - we need to communicate our expectations clearly and in case fleet cannot improve the situation inform the fleet about us taking action.
## Neither couriers nor fleets are made aware of the mechanisms we use to allocate orders and they are not aware of us using the feature described in the ticket. This may make it harder for them to realise that there is something wrong considering that couriers are not blocked by us. However, in case we ever have any court action that would require us to make full disclosure we will not be able to avoid disclosing information about our order allocation practices. This poses serious reclassification and reputational risks.

My recommendation would be:

# Considering issues raised above the best course of action is not to remove policy for low AR couriers, however, since the situation in the market does not pose significant risk (these markets are classified as level 2 risk countries) we can proceed with removing the policy for low AR couriers, but revisit the situation in case we will see that the reclassification risk in these countries increases or in case the impact on couriers orders will be significant enough to reveal the practices we use. I therefore completed the [*table*|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xnyrquWBJOHJ0WNKFohWvIii23KQH6fV_1TMeYZ3l-8/edit?gid=19905251#gid=19905251] in a way that we should not remove policy for low AR Couriers in case any of the countries will turn to risk level 3 country.
# We need to consider whether we are able to implement this feature by communicating our expectations to fleets. If we would be able to communicate to fleets that we will use the method described in the ticket unless they can improve the performance of their couriers - that would reduce our reputational and reclassification risks. However, the information about the practices we adopt are highly likely to leak to the public and it may impact other markets.

In any case, this policy removal feature poses some reclassification risk due to us applying restrictions to couriers and also the fact that we do not communicate our expectations and consequences of non-compliance clearly we are subject to accusation of applying unfair business practices.

If the ride takes more than one hour, the ride price is recalculated. However, as we haven’t sent a pre-authorization charge of that amount, the Rider might not have enough funds to pay - in this case, Bolt has to pay the remaining amount to the Driver.

We would like to make an amendment to clause 6.6 of our T&Cs or add a new clause that would state something like:

6.6. A Bolt não se responsabiliza por quaisquer tentativas de fraude, cometidas pelos Utilizadores e/ou Motoristas, no âmbito de viagens cobradas apenas de acordo com a tarifa horária, cujo preço final, para o Utilizador, seja superior a € 70,00 (setenta euros). Assim, a Bolt declara que, para este tipo de viagens, não se responsabiliza caso a cobrança pelo pagamento no cartão do Utilizador não possa ser efetuada.

The goals are:

* Clearly communicate to Drivers that they should end the ride before the end of the second hour.
* Increase pre-authorization amounts to ensure Riders have enough funds.

Additionally, it is essential to consider that both parties utilize the shared data for their own distinct purposes. For example, we understand that Circle K might use the data for activities in which Bolt is not involved. This separation of purposes supports the classification of each party as an independent controller.

Moreover, the principle of joint controllership implies a shared responsibility and decision-making process regarding the purposes and means of data processing. However, in our case, each party independently determines the purposes and means of processing the data within their control.

In light of these points, we believe that maintaining the status of independent controllers is not only consistent with our past agreements but also aligns with the actual data processing practices and purposes of each party.

If we agree on this point, we are happy to accept some of the changes you made to the Data Sharing Agreement and send you an updated version.{quote}

** number of orders
** number of orders where courier marked order as arrived to provider within 200m distance
** number of orders where courier marked order as arrived to eater within 200m distance
* Based on these statistics we assign couriers cohorts
* Cohorts define earning structures for courier on the next week. It means that couriers with higher cohorts will have more money for orders

MDS UPDATE: 

# Basically my research aligns with Lev’s findings. The city is worried that the route data could give rise to personal data and privacy issues connected to the possibility to identify an individual by their moving pattern. However, calling it “too risky” is a bit of an overstatement. 
# The only thing OMF mentions is the connection of MDS data with other data: no specific mention of intermediate points or route data. It seems that the city made the conclusion of “route data being too risky GDPR-wise” themselves.
# OMF recommends cities to be aware of the privacy implications and develop appropriate standards. As one of the solutions, it recommends to minimize the data. The city seems to be shifting this on the market operators: does not want to receive the route data at all.
# Interestingly, in one of the articles attached by Lev, I traced this idea of “MDS + other data = personal data” to CNIL (French DPA) and their research platform. I’ll occasionally do extra research on this in the upcoming weeks, using French prompts in Google Scholar, if this can be traced to some French academic articles reaching any more particular conclusions, or examples of use-cases. 

Until then, in case the team is worried that we are not GDPR compliant, I’d recommend sending out this message to reassure everyone that it’s not too big of an issue:

“MDS in itself does not contain/produce any personal data. The recent discussions do, however, point out that in combination with other data, they could _potentially_ become personal data. For example, in combination with personal identifiers, like user ID, or saved address. The OMF (Open Mobility Foundation), therefore, recommends cities to minimize the data collected and be aware of the privacy risks that the MDS data in combination with other data could produce. The city is worried that route details could give raise to personal data; if someone is using scooter every day from their home address to work, it can be possible to connect the journey details to a particular individual. The risk is very remote and it does not give a raise to GDPR non-compliance. In order to satisfy the requirements from the city, we recommend switching to version 2.0 that removes this data, or if possible, remove the route data from the current version to satisfy their demands.”

Taking Max s = 0.5 (Var = 0.25) (we know pre-dip results, and could do more custom calculation, but now setting most pessimistic results).

Thank you for your request!

If we are talking about Admin comments, you are completely right that leaving comments on every case would clutter the user profiles unnecessarily. Our processes don’t mention leaving comments for each case for a reason, so there is absolutely no need to start adding comments to all cases. If a process and/or the [🌍 Guidelines for leaving comments and internal notes|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/6615970744978] instruct you to leave a comment, then it should be done. If nothing about it is mentioned, then a comment is not required. You can also look at it this way - if you just give out general information to the user, no comment is usually needed. If there is an issue where you conduct an investigation, perform some action with the user’s account, etc., then a comment should be left. But this is a very general and overall approach, and you should always follow what the relevant process says.  

Regarding the possibility of creating a unified KB article for Tier 1 with links to all relevant KB articles - as much as I understand that there are a lot of links and information that exist in different articles, it would not be feasible to create such an article. We have over a thousand KB articles, so the article would be bound to be outdated too often and very difficult to keep updated. However, I do have some good news. Our Quality and Process Excellence teams are planning to work on creating a general ticket-handling process that would be in the KB and would guide agents on what to do with a ticket from start to finish. I do believe that would be something similar to what you described and would make agent lives slightly easier, so stay tuned! 🤩 

If you have any other questions or if there’s anything else we can help you with, feel free to let us know. In the meantime, I am closing this ticket.

Wishing you a nice day! 🙂

Executed query to find the order with non matching master_basket_ids by date, creator type, master_user_id and city_id



{noformat}SELECT o.id AS order_id, MAX(mb.id) AS master_basket_id
FROM glue.ng_delivery.delivery_basket_master_basket AS wrong_mb
         JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_order_order AS o
              ON wrong_mb.id = o.master_basket_id
         JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_basket_master_basket AS mb
              ON abs(date_diff('second', mb.created, o.created)) < 4
                  AND mb.city_id = o.city_id
                  AND mb.order_id IS NULL
                  AND mb.master_user_id = o.master_user_id
         LEFT JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_order_order AS o_other
                   ON mb.id = o_other.master_basket_id
WHERE
        abs(date_diff('second', wrong_mb.created, o.created)) > 4
  AND o.creator = 'provider'
  AND o_other.id IS NULL
GROUP BY o.id, o.created
ORDER BY o.created DESC
    LIMIT 20000;{noformat}

Hello, Sabina, 

sorry for my late reply 😞  I’m sharing information regarding *reverse VAT* for couriers:

Two files are sent to couriers every week:

*Courier report*. This report is intended for Individual Income Tax declaration. It shows the courier’s income and the amount paid to the bank card.

*Weekly additional delivery costs*. This is a bill, not a report. This bill can be of two types:

*A: Bill payee (receiver) - Bolt* and the sender - is a private courier.
It’s considered that a private courier provided the service to Bolt company (Bolt Technology OÜ). This type of invoice is issued the most often. The reports show compensation for waiting time in the restaurants, bonuses and "Additional delivery costs" (marked as "marketplace fee" in the courier's report).

*B: Bill payee (receiver) - a private courie*r and sender - Bolt. 
It’s considered that the courier bought the service from the Bolt company. This happens quite rarely, mostly in the summer (when the customer pays more for delivery than we promised the courier). 

In case A, the reverse VAT liability falls on the company Bolt Technology OÜ (the courier does not need to pay reverse VAT). 
*In case B, the reverse charge VAT is the responsibility of the courier.* More information on how to do this can be found [here|https://www.vmi.lt/evmi/en/pvm-deklaraciju-teikimas] (LT tax inspection institution page). 

So, the courier has to declare and pay the reverse VAT, but in very rare cases (usually in the summer months) and from a very small amount."	

Please let me know if this information can be visible (available) for couriers. 🙏

# "_Offline trip for cash ride_" should be "_Offline trip for_ *_credit card ride_*" In this context, we compensate the driver when they end a trip and the order status incorrectly changes to cancel. As a result, the driver does not receive the fare they are entitled to. Therefore, after verifying the route details in the Admin, if the driver ends the trip at the drop-off or nearby location with the same estimated time and the driver follows the route estimation, we issue full fare compensation and deduct compensation fee to the driver.

# [Ticket|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/393840882] / [Driver|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/5696070] / [Campaign|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/supply-campaign/campaigns/310388?periodId=2647621] / [Checklog|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/supply-campaign/checklog?filter={"limit"%3A50%2C"offset"%3A0%2C"filter"%3A{"period_id"%3A2647621%2C"driver_id"%3A5696070}}&tz=Asia%2FBangkok] 
The driver did not receive the bonus because our system currently only counts trips that are rated 100% in all categories. The Senior Growth Analyst has identified that the issue arose because new regions/categories were enabled after the campaigns had already started. As a result, drivers from Phuket may not have been properly accounted for in the bonus calculations. To address this, local CS needs to manually compensate the affected drivers. Once we receive the list of drivers facing the same issue from the team, we will proceed with their compensation accordingly.

Moreover, we encountered fraud orders that did not fall into the category that should be detected. As a result, drivers will not receive bonuses in that campaign as well. 
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PFI-509059|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PFI-509059|smart-link]
[https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PFI-499239|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PFI-499239|smart-link] 

# Initially, we received advice to ask the rider to clarify the information when a driver forgets to start the trip, as it seemed like a reliable way to confirm the trip details. However, we can streamline this process and reduce CS costs by verifying the route details in the Admin system. By checking if the driver ends the trip at the drop-off or a nearby location, matches the estimated time, and follows the route estimation, we can accurately validate that the trip took place and still ensure that drivers are fairly compensated.

# Price miscalculation refers to instances where the order settings for calculating trip expenses are incorrect, such as when the start day price is incorrectly changed from 35 baht to 25 baht because of the error settings in our system. This is different from issues related to GPS errors or road closures.

# [Order|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/1698876245/881?orderTryId=2067793925] /[Ticket|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/366861824]  
One example of an Incorrect Price Review that required manual compensation occurred when a trip was reviewed by an agent rather than being processed automatically. In this case, the agent marked the reason for the PR as "Ride did not happen (driver)" because the trip covered a short distance and ended without reaching the destination. However, the driver later contacted us to explain that the trip did occur. The rider had changed their mind and decided not to go to the drop-off point, so the driver drove them back to the pick-up location. The rider was willing to pay the full trip expenses. This scenario highlighted an error in the manual review process, which necessitated manual compensation for the driver.

Hi [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e] - I include our thoughts / advice below from the privacy side. {color:#403294}+*In summary*+{color}:

* We have the following *questions* in relation to collecting the personal information of emergency contacts (see section (1) below):
** Why are we collecting details of the relationship between the emergency contact and the user?
** In any of the countries in which Bolt is introducing this feature, are we aware of any _legal obligation_ to collecting emergency contact details?
* *We are otherwise fine with collecting the details of emergency contacts* from a privacy perspective, +provided that+:
** We ensure that we have a system in place to remove / change the emergency contact’s details if they no longer want to be added.
** We include disclaimer wording before the user inputs the emergency contact’s information (we have prepared some wording below, as well as directions on where in the flow to insert it).
* In respect of sharing trip updates with emergency contacts (see section (2) below), we understand this will not be implemented for a while. We have therefore included some preliminary thoughts on this below as a steer, but please keep us in the loop as the feature is developed.

Happy to discuss if you have any questions on this! 🙂 

----

*(1)* +*Collecting the details of emergency contacts*+

*DATA COLLECTED:*

I understand that the personal details of emergency contacts that will be collected are: (1) full name; (2) phone number; and (3) relationship with the user. This seems sensible, and {color:#36b37e}*we are fine with this*{color} from a privacy perspective. 

However, for completeness, can you +confirm why we are asking for details of the relationship with the user+ (particularly where the user has the option to select ‘child’)? The reason I ask is that we need to make sure that we are generally collecting as little personal data as possible, so please confirm that we have an appropriate justification for collecting this specific type of information.

*LEGAL JUSTIFICATION:*

{color:#36b37e}*We should have an appropriate legal basis*{color} to collect this information. In particular, we should rely on Bolt’s +legitimate interest+ in being able to contact someone else in the event of an emergency incident. We can prepare a legitimate interest assessment (i.e., a report to demonstrate that we have properly considered this legal basis) from our side - this does not act as a blocker on proceeding with the feature. 

We should +avoid relying on the consent of the emergency contact+ to process their personal details, as in practice this will be very difficult to collect and evidence.

Just to confirm - in any of the countries in which Bolt is introducing this feature, are we aware of any _legal obligation_ to collecting emergency contact details? 

*RIGHTS OF THE EMERGENCY CONTACT:*

As previously flagged by Gab, we should ensure that we {color:#4c9aff}*have a system in place to remove / change the emergency contact’s details if they no longer want to be added*{color}. We should also make sure that we have processes in place to allow the emergency contact to request access to their data being processed by Bolt, particularly as we do not collect the information directly from them.

*TRANSPARENCY:*

As previously flagged by Gab, we need to ensure that the emergency contact is informed that Bolt is collecting their personal information, as we are legally obligated to do so.

We understand that sending SMS messages to the emergency contacts to inform them (e.g., “_X added you as a trusted contact on Bolt, please press here to object_”) is not a desirable option as this would be too costly. Instead, we therefore strongly recommend that {color:#4c9aff}*the following disclaimer wording should be included on the ‘*{color}{color:#4c9aff}*_1.01_Trusted Contacts’_*{color}{color:#4c9aff} *page (on Figma)*{color}: “_By submitting the details of your emergency contact(s), you confirm that you have notified them about this. Bolt processes the personal data of your emergency contacts based on Bolt’s legitimate interest in being able to contact someone in the event of an emergency incident if it is unable to contact you. For more information on how Bolt processes personal data, please refer to Bolt’s privacy notices:_ [https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/?category=rides|smart-link] ”.

Please note the following in relation to this disclaimer:

* We are legally obligated to inform individuals about the processing of their personal data +before+ the processing takes place. As such, the disclaimer should +at the latest+ be included at the point that the user fills in their emergency contact’s information. We recommend including it on the ‘_1.01_Trusted Contacts’_ page as this means that the user is provided with this information just before they select ‘Add a contact’.
* The core goal of this disclaimer is to ensure that the user passes Bolt’s transparency information over to their emergency contact. Although this is not a perfect means of achieving this, it is the most practical / realistic, and so the first sentence should be included.
* We do not currently have a dedicated third-party privacy notice that fully covers this processing activity. To mitigate the risk here, we recommend including the second and third sentences to cover our bases from a transparency standpoint. We will work on the privacy notices in tandem, but this should not act as a blocker.

[~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] - Did you get a chance to check whether our privacy notices adequately cover Bolt accessing the user’s contacts?

----

*(2)* +*Sharing trip status / updates with emergency contacts*+

I understand that this is still in the design stage, and so is not being rolled-out just yet - +can you confirm the ETA of this+? Nevertheless, I include some preliminary thoughts below.

*DATA COLLECTED:*

I understand that the following information will be collected from both riders and drivers and shared with emergency contacts when the feature is enabled: (1) name; (2) image;(3) live location; (4) pickup and destination - +can you confirm that this is the full list+? Please also confirm whether, in the case of a rider that has enabled the feature, any personal information about the _driver_ (including the driver’s image) will be shared with the rider’s emergency contact (and vice-versa)? As with the above, we need to be mindful that we are not sharing and personal information unnecessarily, and so it would be helpful to confirm the full list.

In any event, when the user first selects this feature, we should ensure that it is {color:#4c9aff}*by default set to ‘Never’* {color}(i.e., the user’s details will never be shared with the emergency contacts, rather than ‘Always’ or ‘At a scheduled time’). This is important as we need to ensure that we are being fully transparent with live sharing and are requiring the user to actively select that their want their details shared.

*LEGAL JUSTIFICATION:*

{color:#36b37e}*We should have an appropriate legal basis*{color} to collect this information. In particular, we should rely on the user’s +consent+, particularly given that the user will be actively made to select when / how frequently their details are shared with their emergency contact.

*TRANSPARENCY:*

As above, we need to ensure that the user is appropriately informed about how Bolt processes their personal information in this context, which needs to take place +before+ the processing takes place. We therefore recommend {color:#4c9aff}*including some disclaimer wording just before the user selects the option of sharing their data with their emergency contact*{color}, which should direct the user to the relevant privacy notice. We can prepare some wording for this when the feature is at a more developed stage - please keep us in the loop in this regard.

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *21 June 2024.*

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,

Bolt

*COMMERCIAL REVIEW* (optional for you to address during negotiation if you deem relevant):

# Clause 2.3 of the MSA + Clause 1 of SMS Service Schedule (Commercial & Legal provision) - Document hierarchy: The clause does not clearly specify the order of precedence for the documents. It would be beneficial for Bolt to have a clear hierarchy of documents in case of any conflict between the provisions. This should be clarified to avoid any potential disputes in the future. Should the hierarchy be: (1) Service Order, (2) Service Schedules, (3) Master Services Agreement (Main Body), unless explicitly stated otherwise in an applicable Service Order?
# Clause 3.2 currently reads as follows: _3.2	The Service Provider has no obligation to issue or sign a Service Order requested by the Service Recipient._ 
We should probably negotiate this to read: “shall not unreasonably 
refuse to issue or sign a Service Order requested by the Service Recipient”.
# Clause 5.1. reads as follows: _5.1 (d)  Service Recipient shall at all times: remain fully responsible for any access or use of a Service by the Service Recipient or its Users._ It is recommended to specify the extent of Bolt's liability, as "fully responsible" might be too broad and could expose the Partner to disproportionate liability. It would be better to limit the liability to the Partner's _“to the extent that such access or use is within the Partner’s control and/ or is a result of the Partner’s negligence or intentional misconduct”._
# Clause 6.1 - It may be more equitable to share the cost of the site survey between both parties, or for the Service Provider to bear the cost, especially if the Service Provider benefits from the survey by gaining knowledge about the site. This would require negotiation.

# Clause 8.1 last sentence - This clause leaves Bolt without guaranteed support after the warranty period. It would be advisable to negotiate terms that ensure continued support.
# Clause 9.4 Invoice dispute period - This clause could potentially limit Bolt's ability to dispute charges after the 45-day period. It would be advisable to negotiate a longer period or remove the automatic acceptance provision.
# Clause 9.6 - Early Termination Charges - This clause could potentially impose significant costs on Bolt in the event of early termination. It would be advisable to negotiate terms that limit the Partner's liability, particularly in relation to circumstances beyond their control.
# Clause 11.2 Confidentiality period should probably be extended to five (5) years to provide better protection for Bolt's confidential information.
# Clause 11.3 - The same extension of the confidentiality period should be applied here.
# Clause 12.1 - The clause should be modified to ensure that the Service Provider must provide notice before suspending or terminating the Agreement. This will ensure that Bolt has adequate time to prepare for any changes.
# Clause 12.1 (a) (ii) - This clause should be modified to ensure that the determination of unusual usage or suspected fraudulent activity is made reasonably and not solely at the discretion of the Service Provider. This will protect Bolt from arbitrary determinations, i.e. replace with ‘upon reasonable determination of the Service Provider’.
# Clause 19.2. Payment obligation during Force Majeure: This clause requires the Service Recipient to continue making payments even during a Force Majeure Event that affects a Service. This could be unfair to the Service Recipient if the Service is significantly disrupted or completely unavailable due to the Force Majeure Event.
# Clause 25 Use of subcontractors of affiliates: The clause should require a Party to notify the other Party before utilizing the services of its Affiliates or subcontractors, to ensure transparency and accountability.
# Clause 3.1 of the SMS Service Schedule: The contract should specify whether the change in price can be unilateral or if it requires the agreement of both parties. If unilateral, it could potentially disadvantage Bolt.
# Clause 3.1 of the SMS Service Schedule: The indemnification clause is broad and may expose Bolt to significant risk. We should consider negotiating a more balanced indemnity clause.
# Clause 6.2 of the SMS Service Schedule: As it stands, this clause gives the Routing Party unilateral power to suspend the provision of its Platform without any liability. This could potentially be detrimental to Bolt if the suspension is prolonged or unjustified.
# Clause 6.3 of the SMS Service Schedule: This clause requires Bolt to comply with certain policies that may be updated from time to time. +Parties to the Agreement+

High Life North (HLN) - Company Number 13534587

Bolt - Entity not specified. 

+Start Date and End Date+

Agreement is to begin and end in July 2024 (provided there is no delay to the Deliverables). 

+Value of the Contract (Clause 2)+

£960 (£800 + VAT)

The Fee (and any Additional Fees) must be paid by Bolt to HLN within 30 days of the Article being published on the HLN website (unless otherwise agreed in writing). HLN reserve the right to remove the Article from the HLN Website in the event of non-payment or under-payment by Bolt.

{color:#ff991f}This clause gives HLN the ability to pull the Article if Bolt does not pay in full and gives Bolt 30 days to pay the Fee. This clause is agreeable and gives Bolt sufficient time to pay. {color}

+Scope of Services Included (aka the “Bespoke Package” aka the “Deliverables”)+

* Feature to introduce Bolt written, designed and published on their website and weekly e-letter
* Search engine optimisation and use of key words to ensure the article ranks well on Google
* Social media coverage: 1 Instagram Reel 

+Termination Rights of Both Parties (Clause 9)+

Either party may terminate immediately by giving written notice to the other party if the other party commits any material breach of its obligations and/or warranties under the Agreement. 

{color:#ff991f}This clause provides that if either HLN or Bolt breaches the Agreement, the other party can write to terminate with immediate effect. This gives as much protection to Bolt as it does to HLN (and in fact HLN have more duties than Bolt) and so this clause is desirable to Bolt. {color}

+Termination Rights of HLN (Clause 9)+

HLN may terminate at any time and for any reason, not giving Bolt less than 7 days written notice.

{color:#ff991f}This clause gives HLN the right to terminate at will, without any breach. Bolt has a similar right (see below). {color}

+Termination Rights of Bolt (Clause 9)+

Bolt may terminate at any stage prior to Instruction, not giving HLN less than 7 days written notice.

Bolt cannot terminate this Agreement after Instruction, unless otherwise agreed in writing. In the event of termination by Bolt, payment will be immediately due and payable to HLN, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

{color:#ff991f}As above, Bolt also has the right to terminate at will, however this right expires when the Deliverables are reviewed and approved. Bolt, therefore, still has a sufficient window between signing the Agreement and final approval of the Deliverables in which to cancel, should it choose to. {color}

+Liability of Bolt (Clause 10)+

Bolt agrees to defend, indemnify and hold harmless HLN and its officers, directors, agents, affiliates and employees, at all times against all claims, proceedings, demands, damages, liabilities and costs (including reasonable legal fees) arising in connection with: (a) a breach of the Agreement by Bolt; (b) the content of the Article; or (c) a contaminated file, virus, worm, or Trojan horse from Bolt.

{color:#ff991f}This clause requires Bolt to pay all costs including legal fees arising from Bolt breaching the Agreement, litigation arising from the content of the Article and viruses arising from files sent by Bolt. In practice, provided that Bolt instructs, replies to correspondence and pays HLN’s Fee in a timely manner, there is little risk to Bolt on (b) and (c). However, please note that Bolt’s liability is monetarily unlimited, so please ensure there is no content that could give rise to litigation in the Article. {color}

+Liability of HLN (Clause 10)+

HLN will not be liable for any loss or damage, direct or consequential, arising out of any failure or delay in publishing the Article or HLN’s failure to perform any other obligation however occasioned, save for direct negligence by HLN. Compensation shall be limited to the Fee paid by Bolt to HLN.

Save for any liability that cannot be limited by law, HLN’s liability to Bolt will be limited to the amount of the Fee paid to HLN by Bolt and HLN shall have no liability to Bolt for any indirect losses.

{color:#ff991f}This clause states that HLN are liable for loss or damage to Bolt caused by direct negligence (e.g: missing the deadline or not writing the Article per Bolt’s instructions), and this is capped to the Fee amount (i.e: a refund).{color}

+Bolt’s Obligations (Clause 3)+

Bolt undertakes to provide HLN with timely instructions and replies to correspondence.

Bolt shall provide HLN with a full and clear Brief. Bolt must comply with any and all deadlines from HLN. It is the responsibility of Bolt to ensure the Article is accurate and correct prior to publishing.

Bolt undertakes to pay the Fee, the Part Payment (25% on Instruction) and Additional Fees (if any).

{color:#ff991f}This clause requires Bolt to instruct and reply to HLN in a timely manner and meet agreed deadlines. It sets out that the responsibility of checking and approving the Article lies with Bolt. Finally, Bolt must pay 25% of the Fee when the Deliverables have had final approval by Bolt (the other 75% being payable within 30 days of HLN invoicing Bolt). {color}

+Obligations of HLN (Clause 4)+

HLN shall produce the Bespoke Package for consideration of Bolt. HLN shall, upon the reasonable request of Bolt, amend the Bespoke Package to meet the requirements of Bolt.

Following confirmation of the Instruction, the Bespoke Package cannot be amended, unless otherwise agreed in writing. In the event that Bolt seeks to amend the Bespoke Package following confirmation of the Instruction, HLN reserves the right to charge any Additional Fees, as appropriate.

Subject to Bolt fully complying with the Agreement, HLN will publish the Article on the HLN Website. The Article shall remain on the HLN Website indefinitely. 

{color:#ff991f}This clause sets out that HLN will produce the Deliverables as instructed by Bolt with the opportunity for review and amendment. Once Bolt has approved, no further instructions or amendments will be implemented. {color}

+Rights of HLN (Clause 4)+

While every endeavour will be made to meet the wishes of Bolt, HLN cannot guarantee that any particular Article will be disseminated. HLN retains full editorial control over the Article.

{color:#ff991f}This is a standard clause for an outlet such as HLN and does not materially affect the Agreement in any way.  {color}

+Governing Law and Jurisdiction+

Terms and Conditions are to be governed and construed in accordance with English law and any dispute shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales. 

{color:#ff991f}Both parties are UK domicilied and this clause is in accordance with Bolt’s desired governing law and jurisdiction.  {color}

+Additional Points of Relevance+

Any errors in the Article must be raised by Bolt with HLN within 7 days of publication, otherwise no correction will be required by HLN. Alternate remedy to correction is reasonable refund of the Fee. 

{color:#ff991f}This clause states Bolt must raise any issues within 7 days of publication by HLN, and either a correction can be issued by HLN or the Fee can be partially refunded. {color}

+Management Signoff+

Not yet specified. 

+Summary+

To summarise, please note the following points: 

# Bolt must ensure that payment is made to HLN within 30 days of publication of the Article. 
# Bolt must pay 25% of the Fee (i.e: £240) to HLN upon approving the Deliverables.
# Bolt cannot terminate after the Deliverables are approved, unless HLN breach the Agreement. 
# HLN are only liable for losses/damage caused by direct negligence and this is capped at £960. 
# Bolt have unlimited liability to HLN should the Article give rise to litigation. Manager signing off should confirm they are comfortable with this, but from legal’s perspective this situation is likely unlikely. 
# Please confirm the Bolt entity entering the Agreement (presumably Bolt Services UK Limited) and management signing off.
# Provided the above terms are agreed, there are no terms that put Bolt at risk or in a legally unfavourable position in the event of a dispute. 

Happy to discuss any of the above further on Slack or on a call if needed. 

Thanks.

Hey [~accountid:6242fffc1da0e10071388193] 

Thanks for the detailed feedback you’ve shared on the suggestion.

To my knowledge, such a feature has not been rolled out in any market globally.

Regarding the ramifications for route deviation:

* Initially, I thought it was appropriate that if a driver should use a different route than the one selected by the rider, the final price of the trip should not change. Such was the case because we’re avoiding the driver overcharging the rider after the preferred route has already been selected. However, there are legitimate reasons for a different route to be taken (as you have now mentioned) and the driver would have to be compensated accordingly if the distance & time of the new route significantly changes the final price.
* In light of this, how about: 

When an element along the preferred route necessitates a legitimate route deviation (e.g traffic jam, road closure, etc), the driver can request a change in route on the app and he must select the appropriate reason for the deviation, ie “road closure”, for example. After that, the rider would get a notification on their app asking them to validate/confirm the route change. If the rider agrees to the change, a message needs to inform the rider that the final price may change/may be higher as the route taken to their destination may be longer/take more time. 

Also, in cases where the driver chooses to deviate but, for some reason, the rider wasn’t able to confirm the change on their app - maybe the ride was requested on behalf of a friend - then the trip needs to immediately be submitted for a price review (the same way a trip would automatically be sent for fraud review if the price is suspiciously high) so that a follow-up about the route taken can be made with the rider before finalising the ride price. 

I know the above may not have covered all possible concerns with the suggested feature, but I’m hoping that as the discussion progresses and more ideas are shared in this thread, we get to a point where the feature has a sound legal basis before proceeding further.

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Seema
For clarification, the price review would be submitted immediately after the trip has been completed.

Hi, 
The law requires banks to develop similar documents in order to fully comply with the regulations of the National Bank.

The document states that Bolt "is empowered to propose the Bank's credit product to customers." That i think means that Bolt has the authority or the right to propose the Bank's credit products but does not mandate that Bolt must do so. This means Bolt is not obligated to offer these products, it merely has the option to do so.

Also, the document states something that is already required by law: Bolt must comply with the regulations for the protection of consumer rights as set by the National Bank of Georgia. This includes ensuring that comprehensive information is provided to customers, which can be a complex and resource-intensive process. If Bolt fails to comply with these regulations, the Bank can be fined by the National Bank of Georgia. The document specifies that Bolt would be liable to reimburse the Bank for any such fines, leading to significant financial risk. 

The fact that we must comply with the rules of the National Bank is already an obligation due to a law.

Therefore, we must handle this data in accordance with GDPR requirements, ensuring proper legal basis, data protection, and respect for data subjects' rights. 

This has several implications:

# *Data Subject Rights*: Agents must have the right to access, rectify, and erase their data. They also have rights related to data portability and to object to processing.
# *Legal Basis for Processing*: We must have a lawful basis for processing these metrics. I suppose it would be legitimate interest.
# *Data Minimisation and Purpose Limitation*: The data collected should be limited to what is strictly necessary for the purpose for which it is processed.
# *Transparency and Accountability*: We must be transparent about how we collect, use, and store this personal data.

Hi [~accountid:62722e092db308007024a425] my input here for the questions in the description:

# In what scenarios is Bolt obligated to refund an order to the user?

There are several things that could trigger an obligation for Bolt as a Merchant to refund a payment. 
a. Right to withdrawal (cool-off in EU, and everything it means) 
b. Non conforming goods/services: This could be due to the goods being faulty, damaged, or not matching the description provided at the time of purchase.
c. Goods/Services not delivered
d. might be other market specific reasons

# For how long would riders have the right to request a refund. i.e. Should we still refund an order if requested after half a year of the order date?

It depends. 

You have the cooling off period in EU plus Member States local consumer laws and Card Scheme Rules, which also cover this from a “chargebacks” point of view.



Visa and Mastercard both specify time limits for filing chargebacks. These timeframes vary depending on the reason code under which the chargeback is being filed. Typically, the deadlines range from 120 to 540 days from the transaction date, but this can differ based on specific circumstances and the nature of the dispute.


Then, you have the limit of time which could come from an internal Refund Policy (which we do not have at Bolt).

I have [this other ticket |https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/LSS-35727]which is basically asking how long we need to wait so we can reject a refund request. However, it also asks about those cases where Bolt took months to determine if a case was fraudulent or not. 

In summary, and in regard to the issue raised in this ticket which comes from our lack of internal refund policy: “From December on, we started using a local entity (Bolt Support Services IT S.R.L). We are, as we speak, getting refund requests from before November. This is causing us to refund orders from Bolt Operations OÜ which creates an extra VAT burden. Tax team has adviced us to stop refunds from before November in order to avoid this. So, we'd like to understand if we are even allowed to stop refunds to users.”

In my opinion it depend on why the refund is requested. If its because a fraud case and Bolt took months to determine if it was fraud or not, the customer should get their refund. 

If this is specifically for Italy, then I’ll say once we have passed the 14 days cooling off period and the local consumer law period for a refund (if not the same as cool-off), we have the right to reject it.

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

Dear  Marchell Botha



*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *17 May 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Thanks [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e] for confirming these points. My responses are as follows:

----

* *Why are we collecting this data* → “_To make it easier for the agent to identify the person who they are talking to. We can limit the options to Family / Friend if it helps_.”

Understood - thanks for confirming. This purpose sounds sensible and should not prevent us from collecting and processing the data.

If it is possible to limit the options to Family / Friends, then +this would be preferable, but only if it does not disproportionately increase the uplift on your side / undermine the goals of the feature+. 

The reason I flagged this point is that the standards / potential penalties for processing the personal information of children are generally higher than for adults, and so if we are identifying an individual as a child when we collect their information then _technically_ we are increasing the risk profile around that information. This being said, if we have a good reason / business case for identifying emergency contacts as children, this should still be fine from our perspective.

----

* *Are we aware of any legal obligations?* → “_Apparently in Malaysia_”

Are we aware of the full list of countries in which this feature will be rolled out, and if so, +how many+ +_legally_+ +_require_+ +Bolt to collect emergency contact details+?

The reason that this is important is not because it will prevent the feature from being rolled out, but because +this will affect the legal basis that we rely on, and therefore the transparency wording that we should use+. 

In particular, if an EEA country legally requires Bolt to collect this information, then instead of Bolt relying on its _legitimate interests_ to do so, Bolt can instead rely on _complying with legal obligations_ to do so (both of which are recognised legal bases under the GDPR). In such cases, the following disclaimer wording would be more appropriate than the wording we previously flagged (which is more relevant to legitimate interests):

“_By submitting the details of your emergency contact(s), you confirm that you have notified them about this. Bolt processes the personal data of your emergency contacts_ {color:#ff5630}_to comply with its legal obligations_ {color}{color:#ff5630}-_based on Bolt’s legitimate interest in being able to contact someone in the event of an emergency incident if it is unable to contact you_-{color}_. For more information on how Bolt processes personal data, please refer to Bolt’s privacy notices:_ [https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/?category=rides|smart-link] ”.

----

* *Can you confirm the ETA?* → “_No ETA yet, we will aim to have the first version by August_”

Understood - thanks!

----

* *When the feature is enabled, will any driver data be shared with the rider’s emergency contact (and vice-versa)?* → “_Driver Name, Profile Picture, Trip Details, Car Details. This will be available in a link for 6 hours. It’s the standard approach for the Trip Sharing feature_”

Ok - thanks for confirming. Since this part of the feature won’t be rolled out for a while, +let us take this point away and consider it+, as this may raise some additional privacy risks - we will get back to you. In the meantime, my immediate thoughts are as follows:

* As noted in our advice below, we need to be mindful that we are not sharing any personal information unnecessarily, and that we have a valid justification for doing so. Although I can appreciate the importance of sharing the trip details with the emergency contact in real time, sharing other data points in real time (e.g., the driver’s profile picture) may be harder to justify from a privacy perspective.
* We need to ensure that drivers +and+ riders are informed at the appropriate time that their location may be tracked in real time while on a ride. This will require a bit more thought if they have not been the one to actively to choose to share their location during a specific journey (e.g., where a _rider_ has actively chosen to share  journey details with their emergency contact, we need to make sure that the _driver_ is sufficiently notified of this).
