Hi Team - just jumping in from the privacy side. I have included some action items in {color:#36b37e}*green*{color} and some questions in {color:#4c9aff}*blue*{color}.

----

Regarding *Question 1* – to add to [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad]'s comments below:

* The GDPR requires that we inform individuals about the fact that we are collecting their personal data (including account data such as email, name and phone number) +*before*+ it is collected. In other words, we should be informing Romanian users that we are processing their data +*at the latest*+ when the Romanian users register on the platform (i.e., before the user provides any of their personal information, including their phone number).
* The most practical means of achieving this will be to {color:#36b37e}*provide the users with a link to the relevant Romanian / rides-specific* {color}[{color:#36b37e}*privacy notices*{color}|https://bolt.eu/en-ro/privacy/?category=rides]{color:#36b37e} *before the user creates an account*{color}. Are you able to {color:#4c9aff}*provide me with access to the relevant Figma pages / whatever the users will see when they sign up*{color}, so that I can advise on where the link should be included (together with some text to accompany it)? Also, {color:#4c9aff}*I assume the ‘users’ that we are discussing here are both drivers* {color}{color:#4c9aff}*_and_*{color}{color:#4c9aff} *riders*{color}?
* Just to confirm – in the context using phone prefixes to check a user’s T&C eligibility – {color:#4c9aff}*is the user directly providing us with this prefix*{color}{color:#4c9aff} {color}{color:#4c9aff}*as part of the registration process*{color}{color:#4c9aff} {color}(e.g., by typing in their phone number) or are we tracking it automatically (i.e., when the user visits the registration page on their phone, Bolt is already reviewing the user’s phone number before the user has entered any details to determine in which country the user is located?). I assume it is the former, but please confirm.

----

Regarding *Questions 2 and 3* – I cannot advise on the _most effective_ method(s) of checking for T&C eligibility. However, I understand from discussions on this ticket that we are considering using GPS data to do so – {color:#4c9aff}*is this confirmed*{color}? If so, {color:#4c9aff}*how will this work in practice*{color} (e.g., if the user opens up the Bolt registration platform on their computer for the first time, does Bolt automatically track their GPS location data to check whether they are in Romania?). Processing GPS data raises the following issues that need to be considered:

* *Data minimisation*: Applicable laws require that Bolt must use the +*least intrusive means possible*+ to determine whether the user is in Romania. Collecting live GPS data would obviously be a more intrusive means of determining that a user is in Romania than, for example, asking the user to select their country or entering a phone number prefix – however, if this is the only _practically effective_ means of determining the user’s country (and we ensure that we are at all times collecting the minimum amount of GPS data needed for this purpose), then this is something that we can consider.
* *Legal justification*: We need to ensure that Bolt has an appropriate legal basis for collecting this data. Consent, for example, is unlikely to work here if we are automatically collecting the user’s GPS data when they visit the registration page. It appears that Bolt might have a +*legitimate interest*+ in processing such data, but I would need responses to the questions above before I can consider this fully.
* *Transparency*: Our privacy notices currently outline in a very general sense that we may collect location data to provide Bolt’s services to users. However, users are unlikely to expect that Bolt will be using their GPS location data when they visit the registration page, and so it would be worthwhile {color:#36b37e}*including some disclaimer wording on the registration page*{color} (which can be coupled with the link to Bolt’s privacy notices) to ensure that Bolt is being as transparent as possible. I can prepare some wording on this once the above questions have been clarified.

* Requestor is a driver in Romania (Marinache). ID of requestor has already been verified.

We have acknowledged the request, but requestor seems to want access urgently.
* There are 9 messages in total on the chat, 4 of which have been deleted. All messages are from the rider to the driver (i.e., the requestor), and show increasing agitation towards what appears to be the driver not turning up. The final message to the driver is abusive and threatening: “_Fuck you, Marinache. I'm gonna go home, get in my car and run into you. I won't catch you in traffic. I was waiting for you with my family. Fmm you butcher for 10 lei”._

** ANALYSIS **

* The chat can be regarded as the requestor’s personal data, insofar as they can be identified as the recipient of the messages, the requestor is identified by name in several messages, and the messages concern a ride for which the requestor was a driver.
* The messages do not contain any personal data relating to the rider - the messages themselves and the rider’s name comprise the rider’s personal data. We cannot redact the messages themselves, as these are also the requestor’s personal data, and so the main information to be considered for redaction is the rider’s name. Redacting this could be a sensible approach, but then again, the requestor will have already previously seen this information, and so we are not mitigating much harm by redacting this data.
* {color:#36b37e}*Proposed approach*{color}*:* Disclose the messages / time stamps to the requestor, but redact / remove all other personal data of the rider (i.e., the rider’s name).

This week I have received from the local micromobility team a notification dated from May to provide a document to court. I was not aware of the case and therefore called the court the day after.

*Unfortunately, the court confirmed to me that* +*Bolt Support Services has been summoned in February to present a defence in a damage claim and has not responded. The local team started searches in their archive and retrieved the original summons.*+



*What is this case about* 

On *05-05-2022*, the Plaintiff was the victim of an accident. She was hit by a scooter belonging to Bolt and driven by a user that was carrying a second person. The user, the second person, Bolt and the insurance company are all defendants on this case.

The Plaintiff suffered serious injuries and was hospitalised in intensive care for months, initially in a coma. The Plaintiff suffered a traumatic brain injury, loss of cognisance and amnesia for what happened, as well as thoracic trauma with fracture of the left clavicle and multiple fractures of the costal arches and risk of costal volley with bilateral haemopeumothorax.

[^CITACAO.pdf]

*What is the financial risk*

The Plaintiff is requesting the sum of €50,000.00 as compensation for non-pecuniary damage, as well as the amount that will be calculated for the treatments she will have to undergo that are not covered by the Public Medical System and the differences between the wages she would have earned and what she received as a result of the accident at work, paid by AGEAS, and in the future the difference between the contribution and the disability pension.

*What are next steps*

* Respond to the request of the court to submit a copy of the insurance policy and consult the file. [~accountid:712020:430ebb39-7e93-404f-8bdb-62aa9c75ce08] has all the documentation and will take over this file as I will be OOO in the next 2 weeks. * After consultation and a summary from the outside attorney we will have a better understanding of the risks, since in principle the other parties are likely to have contested which will benefit Bolt even though no defence as been presented. 
* There are currently no global processes regarding post mail and documentation management. Locally there is a process, which should be improved to avoid situation such as the one in the present ticket to happen again. I escalated this matter to [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] as well and IMO the ownership of such processes should be with office management globally, including creations of internal tickets. There are documents with confidential and personal data shared through photos or scan apps in slack (and there are no professional machines in the office to scan and copy), documents that are not discarded correctly (leading to fines from the city municipality), documents received with no record being made (which can get lost or remain in the office desks for months). By way of update [~accountid:5d7785151e81950d2d820bda] ,

I need to go through the data received from engineers and amend the data etc.

** SUMMARY OF DSAR **

* Requestor is a [UK driver|https://admin.bolt.eu/fleet/Drivers/driver/1579092] (Raifu). ID has already been verified.
* DSAR submitted on 2 July. Deadline is *2 August*.
* Requestor has requested full order details in relation to a specific [trip|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/514760608/925854303], in order to be able to appeal a penalty charge.
* Requestor already has access to the driver portal (and we have previously directed him to the same). However, requestor has complained that “_it’s been difficult to get the full details of this job on my desktop and couldn’t get it also in my Bolt Apps_” and “_The reason why I requested for the customer details was that it does not shows in my portal, it’s showing just a brief information and not the full details and it will not help enough to make an appeal against the penalty charge notice_”. As such, requestor appears to be submitting a DSAR for *order details beyond what is available on the driver portal*.

** ANALYSIS **

* There a potentially a few issues with this request:
** (1) If certain details about an order are not already available to drivers through the driver portal, I assume that Bolt has a reason for withholding this information, and therefore there may be good reasons not to disclose it in response to the DSAR.
** (2) Requestor seems to be specifically frustrated that they cannot access “_customer details_” about the order. This may suggest that requestor is primarily concerned  the personal data of other individuals (which we are not required to provide).
* My concern with extracting the details of the order and then redacting any third-party personal data and commercially sensitive information is that requestor will likely be left with the information that they can already access through the driver portal. As such, +*responding to the DSAR in the most direct way may not satisfy the requestor*+.
* {color:#36b37e}*Proposed approach*{color}: Request further information from the requestor on exactly what data is missing from the driver portal / exactly what they want that they do not already have (currently, they are just demanding “_full details_”). If we then cannot provide this information (e.g., because it is the personal data of another person), we will be in a position to explain why to the requestor, and hopefully close this off. 

** QUESTIONS for* [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] ***

* Do you agree with the {color:#36b37e}*proposed approach*{color}, based on your previous experience with these kinds of DSARs?
* Beyond data protection requirements, are there any laws that require us to disclose the full details of an order to a driver on request? Do we ordinarily provide full order details in response to DSARs as a result of this?
* What are the next steps in terms of the process for resolving this DSAR?

Hi [~accountid:712020:716b98b3-eb3b-4a3d-b8d8-bbaef921c1be] below feedback on this matter:

* +“Medicinal Products” as classified by the Medicines Authority can include both products that may be dispensed over the counter (OTC) as well as those that can only be dispensed with a prescription (POM)+.
** We confirm that all authorised products bearing the Panadol brand of “paracetamol” are currently classified as an over the counter OTC medicinal product in Malta.
** With reference to ibuprofen however please note that not all Medicinal Products with “ibuprofen” as an active ingredients are OTC, as some are classified as Prescription Only Medicine and therefore this will depend on the specific product itself.
* +The Medicines Act provides that regardless of the classification type, (Article 76(1)), a Medicinal Product shall only be prepared or dispensed from a pharmacy and by a pharmacist+.
** The act of “dispensing” is in turn defined as the sale or supply of medicinal products from a pharmacy. Moreover, Article 79(2) provides that “Unless otherwise provided by or under this Act, a Medicinal Product shall only be sold from a pharmacy.” 
** We are also aware from no-names calls and meetings with the +Medicines Authority+ that they +consider the delivery process as an extension of the dispensing of the medicinal product and therefore all the pharmacy functions are deemed extended to the final point of delivery to the patient.+
** We are not aware of any provision that can be considered as an exception to this rule that would allow a third party such as Bolt to carry a Medicinal Product and act as the party dispensing the medicinal product to the patient.
** The Medicines Act also specifies strict rules for the storage of medicinal products under the charge of the managing pharmacist up until dispensing. Article 85(2) in fact provides that a managing pharmacist cannot permit any medicinal product under his charge to be kept or stored outside his pharmacy and he has to ensure that medicinal products are stored in accordance with storage recommendations.
** We believe that +the current regulatory requirements cannot allow Bolt to operate using the model we are accustomed to see+ i.e. that of the Pharmacy passing on the product (in this case the Medicinal Product) to the Bolt Courier, and having the Bolt Courier in turn delivering it to the client +as the pharmacy has to remain responsible until the act of dispensing the Medicinal Product+.
** These problems arise just from the delivery aspect of the service however, there are other problems that arise in the first phase of the sale process i.e. with the online order aspect. +Online sale or sale at a distance, of medicinal products is not foreseen by the local legislation and there is no licensing regime applicable for it+.

 Please let us know is any questions remain. Thank you

Back in April 2024, we received a request for the following information on the taxi operations from the Transportation Regulator in PT (AMT):

* Terms and conditions in force (on this date), including all versions that have been publicised by BOLT, especially taking into account the point relating to the "Price of the Journey";
* Number of taxi drivers joining the service;
* Monthly invoicing figures for this type of service since the date of entry into operation (indicate dates of entry into operation);
* Written conditions or other information/documents proving the programming (of the algorithm, other) to comply with the rules applicable to the public taxi passenger transport service established by Decree-Law no. 101/2023 of 31 October, namely the fare regime and respect for the geographical organisation and separation of revenue and journeys associated with taxi and TVDE services.

We were not provided with details of the reasons behind the request and submitted the requested information to the regulator: [^Response Bolt_AMT request of information.pdf] 

On June 12th 2024 we received by email a memo from AMT regarding taxi operations, with a request to suspend the service for 30 days:  [^Ofício nº 04389_07JUN_Bolt (2).pdf] During this same time, we were provided with the following instructions:

* Modify the price regime established in the platform for taxi operators, to ensure alignment with the rules for price formulation in DL 101/2023
* Take measures to ensure segregation of services in the platform to ensure passengers clearly understand the differences between TVDE and Taxi (namely in terms of price, territorial cap and accounting).
* Take measures, namely through the re-programming of the algorithm for ride allocation to ensure continuous compliance with geographical boundaries of taxi
* Delete from T&C all provisions (a) that totally exclude Bolt’s responsibility towards passenger and taxi operator (b) allow modifications to t&c depended on their reasonable opinion and (c) other clauses that are absolutely or relatively prohibited.
* Ensure the effective exercise of passengers rights, through Livro de Reclamações, that should be visible and accessible
* Send to AMT in the following 30 days *(DEADLINE TO RESPOND TO THE AMT IS 12TH JULY)*:
** Revised t&c
** Evidence of segregation in the app
** Evidence of modifications in the algorithm

By June 18th the category in the mainland was suspended.

On June 21st, the AMT requested the service to be suspended in Madeira as well. Even though the scope of AMT is national, that seems to be limited by the attributions and competences of the governmental bodies of the Autonomous Region of Madeira. In this region there is a different regulator (DRETT) and therefore we requested both regulators to clarify the scope of their responsability, given the legal framework in place: [^Bolt-requerimento-AMT.pdf] [^Requerimento DRETT (1).pdf]

*INVESTIGATION OF MEANS OF REACTION AGAINST REGULATOR INSTRUCTIONS*

*Background*

AMT instructions are issued under Article 36 of the AMT Bylaws, which provides for the issuing of "binding instructions" (“_instruções vinculativas_”). The law does not provide for any specific regime applicable to binding instructions, except for establishing that acts carried out by regulated entities in breach of binding instructions are null and void and establishing administrative sanctions in the event of non-compliance. In addition, they do not fall into the category of precautionary or remedial measures (“_medidas cautelares_”), which are provided for differently in Article 37 of the Bylaws.

 Precautionary or remedial measures may be adopted without the prior hearing of the addressee, if it would seriously jeopardize their purpose or effectiveness. However, the same possibility is not provided for in relation to binding instructions. Therefore, the adoption of binding instructions without Bolt's prior hearing is in our opinion likely to affect their legality.

 Under Article 43(2) of the AMT Bylaws, the activities of AMT that have an administrative nature are subject to administrative jurisdiction. Consequently, in the absence of special rules applicable to this procedure, the general administrative legislation is applicable.

*Means of reaction*

 The means of reaction against AMT instructions are:

* Submission of a formal complaint to AMT within *15 days* (“reclamação graciosa”) under Article 191(3) of the Code of Administrative Procedure. This complaint does not automatically suspend AMT’s instructions. However, the Code of Administrative Procedure allows for Bolt to request AMT the suspension of the effects of the instructions (Article 189(2)).
* Filing of an injunction before the administrative court asking for the suspension of the effectiveness of the AMT instructions (which must be followed by an administrative action within 3 months). The suspension of the effectiveness is automatically given by the court until a final decision in the main proceedings (administrative action) is issued. However, AMT can file a motion against the suspension of the effects of the injunction on grounds of public interest; once this motion is filled by AMT, the injunction can no longer prevent the execution of AMT's instructions (the motion can be challenged, but only after a courts decision regarding the challenge of the motion will the suspension be resumed).

Given the limitation of effective means of reaction, it was decided to attempt a delay in the Madeira request for suspension by requesting a clarification to both regulators on their scope of responsability. Additionally, Bolt will provide the response within 30 days.

*DEADLINE TO RESPOND TO THE AMT IS 12TH JULY*

From a risk perspective, incentives based on performance can be tricky as they might be used against us. Courts in different countries have found that  incentives that require the courier to always be online, always continuously accept orders etc (e.g. based on acceptance rate) can be seen as a way of controlling the courier (which means they might be seen as our employees)Right now, the “number of orders in a week” is something that could in theory be used against us. It’s not as risky as “acceptance rate”, but since the couriers have to achieve a certain number of orders within a limited time (i.e. 1 week if they want higher base pay the next week - at least I assume that’s how it works, the number of orders doesn’t accumulate over a long period)? To de-risk it, the “number of orders” that is counted should not be related to a fixed time period - but I understand then this kind of loses it’s point 
The “distance from eater/merchant” cohort is less risky - since we can claim that pushing “arrived” as close to the merchant/eater as possible is necessary for our algorithm to work and show correct ETAs/ensure food quality.

Bolt retains your data for only as long as necessary for the purposes described above. This means that we retain different categories of data for different periods of time depending on the type of data, the transportation service it relates to, and the purposes for which we collected the data.

*_Automated decision-making if you are a user of the rental services_*



*What personal data do we process?*



When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, ie. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions. 



*How do we process your personal data?* 



Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.



If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings: 



# *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehavior; 
# *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and 
# *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.



For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

*_Automated decision-making if you are a user of the rental services_*



*What personal data do we process?*



When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, ie. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions. 



*How do we process your personal data?* 



Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.



If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings: 



# *first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehavior; 
# *second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and 
# *third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.



For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

Process for CS at the DEC.

Update personal information/ documents

# Ask the driver if they made this request via support in app, and find out why it wasn’t updated in that instance.
# Check if the documents that need updating are up-to-date, legitimate, and if they are legible. 
# Update information/ documents in Admin.

Balance/ commissions

# Check if all the bank account information provided is correct. 
# Update information if needed.
# Educate drivers.

Category change, Car to motorcycle/ Motorcycle to car.

# Make sure all documents are legitimate and up to date.
# Check if the commission is zero.
# Update documents if needed.
# Request OPS team for help to finish changing the category.
# Educate drivers on how commission in this new category works, safety measures.

Blocked accounts

* Identification verification failed
1. Ask for all the physical documents, make sure they are legitimate.
2. Double-check why they failed the verification process. 
3. If the issue for failing the process is system error, camera quality, bad state documents, CS will ask OPS team to send a new verification.
4. If the issue for failing the process is Faces don’t match, Different devices + distant locations, Attempted Deceit Printout Used, CS will inform the driver that their account will not be unblocked. 
* Infinite blocks when auto-accepted
1. Check the blocking reason in the comments section in Admin.
2. Analyze if the documents provided are legitimate. CS team will need to examine the physical documents to be sure. 
3. Ask for new pictures of vehicles and pictures of vehicle plates.
4. If the documents and information provided are correct, CS will lift the block.

We had 3 principle consideration points:

(1) cash pooling on biggest scale efficiently worked until regulators were accepting IC receivables as sufficiently reliable asset for the purpose of entity level capital calculation. When Wise (mainly EMI entities) started to get regulatory pressure (as IC assets are not always treated as reliable because of related nature of the parties) multi day cash pooling was reducing over time

>> below is relevant for product related assets, which having fast turnaround cycle. NOT relevant for fully internal assets (ones which are fully segregated from product ones, and any CROSS movement has very strict pre-defined reasons like: margin extraction, operational buffer investment, operational buffer withdrawal,…)

we justified two sub-use cases:

(2) liquidity transfer and planning. when company makes explicit transfers of asset X to account A in any other entity for purpose of conducting scheduled business activities (exchange, hedge, payout, safeguard, etc.). Wise was making these transfers in accordance with liquidity management policy with clear defined metrics, logic of calculation, balances, rules for exceptions etc.

(3) rather pooling into several liquidity hubs (EU, APAC, AMERICAS, etc.) with very similar goal - to fund explicit business activities in accordance with clear schedules (does not matter if daily or weekly).



in both (2) and (3) - if done correctly AND when amount of asset buffer in product asset scope ( = total cash in product scope - total liabilities to users, partners) is justified in accordance with collection dynamics and payout dynamics) - it is pretty easily possible to justify that within short period of time (day/week/…) liquidity is turning (something comes, something leaves, etc.). Also in the period of positive CB rates entity which earns interest on assets either fully or partially should be paying those back (VAT exempt usually though) and charge other entities for liquidity management services (also usually VAT exempt). 

As a result: 

* product facing assets in “pools” or “liquidity hubs” are rather held / managed, but not treated as loan BECAUSE entity in reality can’t benefit from those itself.  Entity is providing very particular liquidity management service. (achieved via same evidenced product <> internal asset buckets strict segregation = no comingling)
* TP becomes very simple / monthly basis only with no need to argue on rates to be applied for different assets / jurisdictions / etc.

As we are heading towards EMI license(s) step by step - we would need to ensure these basic rules are covered in future EMI setup very strictly.  But no one stops us from maturing our liquidity segregation and management right away.

{color:#0747a6}*On the first question* {color}- I had a look into articles 6.1 and 6.2 of the tender notice and below are my thoughts. 

* The Operator should comply with fleet sizes as stated in section 6.1 which range between 3000 and 6000 vehicles. 
* However the operator *can request (and the City must approve it) either to increase or decrease then number of vehicles* +twice a year+ submitting a request to the City of Paris: 
** +by 1st March t+o request a change for the Summer period (April to end October
** +by 1st October+ to request a change for the Winter period (November to end of March). 
* The Operator can also request to increase the fleet beyond the maximum size allowed of 6000 vehicles: 
** +*During the first year,*+ the operator can request the City of Paris to increase the fleet up to 9000 vehicles if ti can prove *average RPV over 30 consecutive days is higher than 4.*  The City can refuse the request or accommodate the request. In the latter case, the fleet increase can be done the month following the approval from the City. 
*** The tender notice is unclear but it seems that the increase will apply for a period or in the best case scenario for the remaining months of the first year.
** +*During the following years, the City can*+ authorise, for each period (Summer  OR Winter or Year Y), a fleet increase of 3,000 additional vehicles (max 9000 vehicles), if the operator can prove *average RPV over* +*2*+ *30-day consecutive periods of the same period of Y-1 is higher than 4.*  The increase will be then authorised for each period Summer/ Winter.
* My understanding is that the City can accept to increase the fleet up to 9000 vehicles but for limited period of time and Operator can submit a request to decrease it, subject to specific deadlines to apply for the decrease (see 2nd bullet point above). 
* *According to Q&A no. 40* we fleet sizes to be inserted in Annex 4 ‘Provisional business plan’ (_Plan d’affaires prévisionnel_) should be within the bracket of 3000 - 6000 vehicles and *should not* account any request for increasing the size up to 9000.

Hi Carolina,

For context, the Spanish team used to produce loss of profit certificates for some fleets to claim loss of profits from their insurance. For example, when one of the fleet's vehicles was being repaired and couldn’t provide transportation services, they needed a “certificate” from Bolt stating how much the vehicle in question made per day to claim the loss of profit for the days the car was inactive. While I wasn’t a fan of issuing these certificates, the business really wanted to support the fleets.

Occasionally, these claims against insurance companies end up being disputed in Court, with judges asking us to confirm or clarify certain points in the certificates.

We have a template to respond to these Court requests (attached), so I recommend reusing and adapting it on a case-by-case basis.

Here’s the process I suggest:

# Put the response in a Google Doc and tag the relevant business person (in this case, Marc) to confirm the details we should include.
# Refine and polish Marc's input.
# Once finalized, send the response via email (sample email attached) to the Court with Marc cc’d.
# Also, ask Andrea Figueroa (Spanish Office Manager) to send a hard copy via post to the Court along with a copy of the _“oficio.”_

Happy to discuss further if needed.

Many thanks!
